---
title: "Evaluation under an alternative posterior law"
subtitle: "2.17 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 16 and 18"
description: "Fixed-report risk and regret under distinct selection and evaluation laws."
---

The posterior used to choose a report may differ from the law used to evaluate it. Here the selection law remains
fixed while the evaluation mean of one site, or all evaluation standard deviations, are varied. The selected report
is held fixed and scored under both laws. Its evaluation risk is also compared with the minimum under the evaluation
law over the same report family. This separates a change in the risk of a given report from regret relative to an
alternative report. Neither specified law is assumed to describe an external population exactly.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Same laws.** The selected report has risk .0417 under either law, and evaluation regret is 0. The plotted
  intervals and means coincide; the largest pair-error gap is also 0. This is the point from which each
  disagreement can be read.
- **Move C upward.** The frozen report's evaluation risk rises to .1360, while the evaluation-best report has
  risk .0542. Their difference, .0817, is the regret. The chosen reports change 3 pair decisions. The table separates the two evaluations of each report.
- **Wider evaluation law.** The frozen report now has risk .0779, yet regret remains 0. It is still best in the
  family under the evaluation law. A change in the risk of a report does not by itself imply that another
  report should replace it.
- **C +.40, no cap.** Evaluation regret is .0108. Both optimisations now search the larger family; the family
  tags identify their common comparison domain. The bound keeps this family fixed while changing the law.
- **Small change, new report.** A pair-error radius of .0132 accompanies 1 changed pair decision. Regret is
  only .0008, beneath the uniform bound .0263. A small objective gap can coexist with different grade vectors.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The laws here are independent normals specified for teaching. Neither is asserted to be the true law of an
external population. The general bound is twice a justified uniform risk-discrepancy bound plus a valid optimiser
gap over the whole common family. That gap concerns selection-law optimisation and is zero here; evaluation
regret concerns the other law. Exact enumeration supplies the selection-law minimum; more posterior draws cannot
establish agreement between the laws.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
g <- c(A=1L,B=1L,C=2L,D=2L,E=3L,F=3L)
postrank_evaluate(g, pr_tutorial$one, weights=c(score_A=1), tau=.2)$weighted_risk # .04165164
```
:::

Standalone: [two evaluation laws](../../embed/another-law.html), for example `?shift=1&unit=C`.

Related applications: [Reporting risk and withholding cost](price-of-silence.qmd),
[Monte Carlo error in pairwise probabilities](../uncertainty/mc-error.qmd).
